description.text: Notion is a software development company headquartered in San Francisco that provides a unified, highly customizable workspace consolidating planning, team knowledge, notes, workflows, and collaboration into one platform.

industry.text: Notion operates in the software development industry, specifically in workspace productivity and collaboration software.

products_services.text: Notion offers an all-in-one customizable workspace platform where teams can manage project roadmaps, wikis, meeting notes, workflows, and use integrated AI tools for writing, brainstorming, code, search, and workflow automation.

customer_segments.text: Notion primarily targets enterprise customers including departments such as product, HR, marketing, and IT, with usage by 98% of Forbes Cloud 100 companies and 62% of Fortune 100 companies.

geographic_presence.text: Notion is based in San Francisco, California, United States, with a global enterprise customer base.

funding.text: Notion has raised approximately $418 million in total funding across 9 rounds, with the latest Series D round in September 2021 raising $275 million at a $10 billion valuation.

recent_developments.text: In September 2026, Notion acquired the Indian startup Automate.io to accelerate product expansion and enhance integration capabilities with over 200 services.
In 2025, Notion launched an AI agent product and crossed $500 million in annual revenue, reflecting significant growth and adoption of AI-driven workplace productivity features.

positioning_usp.text: Notion positions itself as a customizable, all-in-one AI-powered workspace that integrates team knowledge, workflows, and collaboration with enterprise-grade security, governance, and integration capabilities, trusted by a vast majority of Forbes Cloud 100 and Fortune 100 companies.

## Insights

**Enterprise scale** Notion operates with 5001-10000 employees and generates substantial revenue, indicating a large enterprise footprint and potential for upsell to advanced collaboration, governance, and security features suitable for enterprise-wide deployments.

**All-in-one appeal** As a versatile all-in-one workspace that consolidates product roadmaps, wikis, meeting notes and workflows, Notion presents opportunities to upsell teams into broader use across departments such as product, HR, marketing and IT.

**Tech stack fit** Notion already leverages a breadth of tools (MongoDB, Intercom, New Relic, Marketo, Greenhouse, Asana) suggesting receptivity to integrations and automation; sales motions can emphasize seamless data flows and integration capabilities with customers' existing stacks.

**High growth signals** With revenue in the high billions and a substantial funding round, Notion is in a growth phase with budget for expansion, migrations, and enterprise features, presenting timing for expansion selling cycles and premium support offerings.

**Competitive landscape** Notion sits among strong productivity and collaboration rivals; targeting enterprises already evaluating or using similar platforms (Asana, monday.com, Trello, Airtable) offers a clear path for differentiation through deeper customization, security controls, and centralized knowledge management.

But unlike most startups that have boomed with the rise of generative AI, Notion hasn't raised outside capital in a long time. Its most recent fundraising round came in 2021, when the big driver for cloud-based collaboration software was the Covid pandemic and remote work. In October of that year, Notion raised $275 million at a $10 billion valuation.

Kothari says the company has more cash on hand than the $330 million it's raised to date. [...] Weeks after Notion's big financing round in 2021, Microsoft announced Loop, an app for working on documents. The product, which resembles Notion, became available to organizations with Microsoft 365 productivity software subscriptions in 2023.

Microsoft is also pushing Copilot, an AI assistant that can spit out Word documents and Outlook emails. Google, meanwhile, offers the Gemini AI option for its Google Workspace applications. [...] Notion was founded in 2013, two years before OpenAI was created as a nonprofit AI lab. The company, which now has about 1,000 employees, launched the first version of its product in 2016 and says it has over 100 million users.

sources.title: I've tried dozens of Notion alternatives, these are the only ones worth using
sources.excerpt: Docmost is an open-source and self-hosted wiki and documentation platform that feels like a simplified version of Notion. It’s primarily built for collaboration, but it works just as well for solo users. Docmost can run on your own server and also supports encryption, so your documents are completely under your control. It has a real-time editor where multiple people can edit the same page at once without overwriting each other, plus it has diagrams, tables, and even Mermaid and Excalidraw [...] Out of the box, it’s quite minimalist, but probably also not what you’re used to if you come from Notion. The slash command is different, the formatting options are different too, and the architecture overall might take some getting used to. Obsidian does have databases, namely Bases, and they’re much easier to navigate than Notion’s since you don’t need to manually add any properties and just define the rules. [...] Anytype is a Notion alternative I’ve covered extensively before. It’s like working with a Notion clone, except it is offline-first and local-first.
